catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue motion class fits a BCS motor: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 requires joint_positions in rad and a joint order, while the unit, gear ratio and travel range of a BCS motor are deployment configuration read by BCSDeviceManager (General Parameters -> Units) and not carried by BCSMotor. The extension targets the raw configured value with no invented conversion, and its target_position is Limit.operator_required until the site supplies this motor's range.

cap.motion.stop.v1 advertises an optional deceleration in m/s2 (its catalogue example is {deceleration: 2.0}), but BCSServer.stop_motor sends only the motors list and BCSMotor.stop() calls it with the motor name; the BCS server uses its configured stop deceleration. An extension with no input avoids advertising a value the native call cannot honour; it is also the safe_state action.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/als-controls__bcs-ophyd-zmq --backend fake; the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and never a hardware or ROS run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is OphydDriver, but the selected entry bcsophyd.zmq.bcs_motor:BCSMotor is a custom Ophyd Device/PositionerBase over a ZeroMQ client with no classic Component(EpicsSignal, ...) declarations for the OphydDriver profile, so this is a direct Driver with native.py. Covered: fresh GetMotorFull reads of Raw Motor Position and Motor State/Move Complete, the configured unit string, the move extension (MoveMotor plus fresh-state polling), the stop extension (StopMotor plus two consecutive fresh Move Complete reports), and @estop through the same native stop. NOT COVERED: BCSSignal analog inputs (get_freerun), BCSDeviceManager/Happi discovery, and BCSAreaDetector, whose image is a hard-coded 3x3 test pattern (README.md:18 calls it '2D detector support (under development)'), not a camera transport. The move target has no sourced travel range: it is Limit.operator_required and every move is refused until the site supplies site-limits.json; the -5..5 values in site-limits.example.json are examples, not device data. The extension ids are used because cap.motion.joint_position.v1 is specified in rad and joint order (the BCS unit is deployment configuration) and cap.motion.stop.v1's schema/example carries a deceleration in m/s2 that BCSServer.stop_motor cannot accept (StopMotor sends only the motor name; the server uses the configured stop deceleration). The target/position unit is '1': the number is the raw configured unit, treated as dimensionless by MHS, and the field description states this. Fidelity: the fake is a native-shaped in-memory stand-in (F0), not a recording; all canned numbers are placeholders. Native limitations disclosed: zmq_move_motor and zmq_stop_motor run each request in a worker thread and do not re-raise its exception, so a rejected MoveMotor/StopMotor exchange is invisible to the caller; the driver relies on a subsequent GetMotorFull (which does raise) and the stop action reports stopped only after two consecutive fresh Move Complete reports, failing the receipt otherwise. No hardware e-stop, interlock or safety-rated channel is documented in the clone and no estop_physical_ref was invented; BCSServer.bcs_request sets no receive timeout and the single REQ socket is shared without a lock, so the software stop is not a certified safety function. native.py imports bcsophyd (ophyd/happi/pyzmq) and needs a reachable BCS server; it was never opened or run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by is null); at R1 the loader's model-written review refusal (which applies at R2/R3) does not protect this package, and no human reviewed or tested it. The gate reported no warnings; check-report.json is the gate's own report.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation, every fact, the stop path and the fake against bcs_motor.py, bcs_server.py and bcs_device_manager.py at the pin. Unlike the readiness evidence (blocked for OphydDriver reasons), the author found a documented native stop (StopMotor, bcs_server.py:1187-1202), and the stop action reports stopped only on two fresh Move Complete reports, but the stop cannot always be delivered: every request of one BCSServer shares a single ZeroMQ REQ socket without a lock or receive timeout (bcs_server.py:105, 123-148; BCSMotor._lock is created at bcs_motor.py:64-65 and never taken), and zmq_stop_motor swallows a refused send in its thread (bcs_motor.py:412-436). The runtime cancels a running move before the e-stop; when the move waits for a GetMotorFull reply, the cancelled receive leaves the socket waiting, so both StopMotor sends and every later request are refused, StopMotor never reaches the server and the motor finishes its move (review/lists/r22-probe_bcs_req_race.py); the author's fake (instant replies, no REQ state) could not show it. The reviewer changed driver.py (the @estop sends StopMotor, then raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; safe_state, docstring, units and move descriptions; three output units removed; six facts narrowed and seven added, including the licence clause), fake.py (REQ-state knob), test_driver.py (unreached e-stop, StopMotor behind a pending reply, refused MoveMotor still completed) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028 (stable digest sha256:00ab60745ae8ec5f4f22ce6ff652d65ce2e0e93c4a17a92200b2a3f8dc97413c), the eleven package cases pass, and the author's notes describing a pass and the server's configured stop deceleration are superseded. For the human reviewer: One configured BCS motor at R1 (card floor; the move target stays operator_required). StopMotor is documented as sent at once to the motor controller, but the upstream client cannot stop concurrently: one REQ socket, no lock, no receive timeout, refused MoveMotor and StopMotor swallowed in threads, and blocking thread joins inside coroutines on the bridge's event loop, so an unanswered request wedges the driver until restart. A refused MoveMotor still ends completed with the motor unmoved. Unblocking needs every request serialised behind one lock with shielded receives (or a separate connection for StopMotor) and bounded receives that re-create the socket. LICENSE.md is the LBNL BSD form with an Enhancements grant (LICENSE.md:28-37) while the card and pyproject.toml:12 say BSD-3-Clause; the override proposal adds publish_review required.
